title: Meeting Frankie Trumbauer as a boy
summary: Tate tells Trumbauer he owns his records with Bix; he is wearing short pants.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: So I met him and my brother and well, I was kind of -- I think I talked more than my brother, you know, because I was talking to him and I says, I told him that I had their records, "Singing the Blues" he and Bix made, you know, and "The Riverboat Shuffle," and I said I had everything he'd

made. And I told him I had the things by Red Nichols and the Five Pennies, I had all of theirs. So he says, "Really?" I had on short pants -- you know Gary, in those days, you had to wear short pants, you know, until you -- you didn't hardly get a long suit, long pair of pants, until you was maybe 21 years old, until the later years, you know. So I had them on and knicker socks and my brother had on -- you know, he was eight years older. So I talked to him and I said, "I want to meet Bix, too." He says, "Well, you'll meet him." He says, "God knows where he is," he said, "but he'll be here."
